land.text: Delta, Cairo, Giza Nile reach and Faiyum edge: Maadi near Cairo, Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha, Minshat Abu Omar, el-Gerza and Haraga ('about a dozen sites'); the region Lower Egypt without the governorates of Matruh, Al Jizah (but with its Nile reach within 20 km of the river), Alexandria, Ismailia and Port Said, plus the Faiyum; the page never names the Western Desert or the Matruh coast

successors.note: "replaced by the Naqada II culture" at Naqada IIc/d; "by the end of Naqada II circa 3200 BCE".

correction.text: Lower Egypt and the Faiyum: Maadi, Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha; the culture "emerged from the earliest Neolithic sites of the Nile Valley, in the Faiyum region"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. "The Maadian culture is first identified during the second part of Naqada I" (Naqada I is "about 3900-3650 BC" on the Naqada page) and "continued until Naqada IIc/d, when it was replaced by the Naqada II culture"; it "was much less developed than the contemporary cultures of Naqada I and Naqada II" and its pottery and flint have "strong similarities with the contemporary Chalcolithic culture of Palestine". No area figure to compare.

region.text: Delta, Cairo, Giza Nile reach and Faiyum edge: Maadi near Cairo, Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha, Minshat Abu Omar, el-Gerza and Haraga ('about a dozen sites'); the region Lower Egypt without the governorates of Matruh, Al Jizah (but with its Nile reach within 20 km of the river), Alexandria, Ismailia and Port Said, plus the Faiyum; the page never names the Western Desert or the Matruh coast

ledger.note: 3800 BCE: the Maadian culture of Lower Egypt, trading partner of Chalcolithic Palestine. "first identified during the second part of Naqada I", which the Naqada page dates "about 3900-3650 BC"; the year is the midpoint of that phase. The Delta had no culture on the map since Merimde ended c. 4200 BCE. [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: confidence 2 to 1: 3800 is the midpoint of Naqada I, not a year the page gives] Fix fx-50 (3 Nov 2026, R030): region narrowed to the shape of the m3300-m3201 keyframe override (Lower Egypt minus Matruh, Al Jizah, Al Iskandariyah, Al Isma`iliyah, Bur Sa`id, plus the Giza Nile reach and the Faiyum) so that ledger and keyframe agree; page re-read: 'It consists in about a dozen sites, including the excavated cemetery and settlement complex Maadi near modern Cairo'; it names no site in the Western Desert, Matruh, Alexandria, Ismailia or Sinai.

region.text: Delta, Cairo, Giza Nile reach and Faiyum edge: Maadi near Cairo, Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, Tell el-Farkha, Minshat Abu Omar, el-Gerza and Haraga ('about a dozen sites'); the region Lower Egypt without the governorates of Matruh, Al Jizah (but with its Nile reach within 20 km of the river), Alexandria, Ismailia and Port Said, plus the Faiyum; the page never names the Western Desert or the Matruh coast

ledger.note: 3200 BCE: Upper Egypt absorbs the Delta. "The cultures of Lower Egypt were replaced by Upper Egypt and Naqada culture by the end of Naqada II circa 3200 BCE"; "Maadi was first conquered during Naqada II c-d"; "The Maadian culture of Buto, Tell Ibrahim Awad, Tell el-Rub'a, and Tell el-Farkha were vacated", Buto "giving way to the Naqada III culture". [Reviewer xx-01-a, 2026-10-18: confidence 3 to 2: the page names Lower Egypt but places only the Maadian's Neolithic roots, not the culture, in the Faiyum] Fix fx-50 (3 Nov 2026, R030): region narrowed to the shape of the m3300-m3201 keyframe override (Lower Egypt minus Matruh, Al Jizah, Al Iskandariyah, Al Isma`iliyah, Bur Sa`id, plus the Giza Nile reach and the Faiyum) so that ledger and keyframe agree; page re-read: 'It consists in about a dozen sites, including the excavated cemetery and settlement complex Maadi near modern Cairo'; it names no site in the Western Desert, Matruh, Alexandria, Ismailia or Sinai. 'The people of Naqada II and Naqada III seem to have expanded northward into Lower Egypt, replacing the Maadian culture.'

certainty.note: An archaeological culture: the Delta and the Faiyum as regions; the southern limit against the Naqada culture is soft.

sources.title: Naqada culture
sources.note: Phase dates (Naqada I 3900-3650, II 3650-3300 BC) used to place the Maadian start.

notes: Culture dossier. The Maadi page has no infobox and dates only by Naqada phase; the start (3800 BCE) is the midpoint of Naqada I and the end (3200 BCE) is the page's own "circa 3200 BCE". The page is inconsistent on whether Naqada II or Naqada III replaced the Maadian at Buto; 3200 BCE is used. Heliopolis, Wadi Digla, Tell el-Iswid are not on the page. Gazetteer: Maadi, Buto, Tell el-Farkha are not places; the Lower Egypt and Fayyum regions stand in.
